claim: A kiln firing 30,000 bricks a day burns about 4.9 t of coal a day, 30 kg per fireman per round
law: Energy balance 30,000 x 3.0 kg x 1.2 MJ/kg / 22 MJ/kg; cited range 11 to 70 t of coal per 100,000 bricks (poverty.ch, SDC)
check: 16.4 t per 100,000 bricks, inside the cited 11 to 70 t

claim: The hopper holds at least one feeding round of coal for one fireman (R6)
law: Frustum volume of the hopper below the grille x bulk density 0.80 kg/L; holds for the 30,000 a day, two-fireman case (the review noted that at 50,000 bricks a day a round needs about 50 kg, so the hopper then holds 0.84 round and is refilled each round)

claim: A four-pocket rotor meters about 0.49 kg of coal per pocket, repeatable within 15 % (R5)
law: Pocket volume x 80 % fill x bulk density; fill of a rotary valve depends on lump size, moisture and speed
check: 0.770 L per pocket at 80 % fill; repeatability can only be measured (weigh 20 doses, TRL 4)

claim: The bridge carries 1.5 x the 250 kg rated load at mid-span below yield (R3)
law: Simply supported truss over 6,600 mm, chord force = M / chord spacing, S275 yield 275 MPa; proof case 1.5 x 250 kg plus the carriage and its full hopper at mid-span

claim: The guardrail takes the 1.5 kN proof push on the top rail below yield, with the U-frame bearer (R2)
law: Cantilever posts bolted together, end moment into the frame bearer (RHS 60 x 40 x 4); highest of post pair and bearer shown

claim: The bearer end-plate bolts carry the guardrail moment (R2)
law: Elastic bolt group of three M12 8.8 in a column, pivot at the plate's lower edge, with a 1.3 allowance for prying; M12 8.8 design tension about 48 kN; end-plate bending to confirm at TRL 4

claim: The track channel spans 1.0 m between pads under the worst wheel load below yield (R8)
law: UPN 80 about its weak axis, Wy 6.36 cm3 (handbook), wheel load with a 1.25 dynamic factor; pads sit 100 mm each side of every module joint, so a wheel on a joint spans 200 mm

claim: No track wheel carries more than its rating, at the 250 kg rated load (R3)
law: Statics of the deck with the full carriage at its travel limit and the 250 kg rated load beside it, 1.25 dynamic factor (450 kg with the 100 kg fireman); first checked against a 500 kg wheel and refuted by the independent review (621 kg); wheels now specified at 650 kg (D15); rating on a grooved wheel on a round bar and at wall-top temperature to confirm with the supplier

claim: The kiln wall tops carry the track pads (R8)
law: Pad pressure against an interim 0.20 MPa; weak-mortar clay brick masonry prisms 3.5 to 4.7 MPa (Kaushik, Rai and Jain, 2007); hot, old kiln walls to survey
check: 0.151 MPa under a pad against 0.20 MPa interim; the real limit comes from the partner kiln survey

claim: One fireman moves the loaded deck with 200 N or less at the hand wheel rim (R4)
law: Rolling resistance 2 %, 45 mm tread, 160 mm rim radius, chains 85 % (two stages in series may be nearer 72 %); on a 2 % grade, no wind; with a 2 % grade the 200 N is used up at a 5.4 m/s wind (KND-CAL-001 s15)

claim: The lock pin holds the loaded deck on a 5 % grade (R10)
law: The two driven wheels (the side B wheels, which carry the hopper carriage and so more than half the weight) locked and sliding on a dusty round bar at a friction of 0.15; no wind
check: Pull 491 N against a hold of 736 N at friction 0.15 and 491 N at 0.10, so the margin vanishes if the bar is very dusty or oily; friction of a locked wheel on the bar can only be measured (TRL 4)

claim: The insulated floor keeps the fireman's feet far cooler than the bare crust he stands on today
law: Steady balance: crust radiation (emissivity 0.3 dusty aluminium, 0.9 crust), convection, 37 mm board at 0.065 W/mK, sun on the top sheet; underside emissivity 0.05 to 0.9 gives 72 to 75 C; a coal-dusted top sheet (absorptance 0.9 in place of 0.5) gives 93 C; R7 (50 C) is not met in full sun

claim: The 6 mm track joint gaps take the rail's heat growth
law: Linear expansion 12e-6 /K x 3,000 mm x 100 K (5.0 mm for a 140 K swing from a cold install)

claim: The deck cannot tip across the kiln with the full hopper carriage at its limit
law: Moments about the side B wheel line: deck weight against the carriage overhang

claim: The metering crank turns with a light hand force
law: Janssen pressure of coal on the rotor (friction 0.5, K 0.4) x rotor friction at the rim / 140 mm crank; hydrostatic head with no wall relief as an upper bound; a 40 mm lump jamming at a vane tip, and wet coal arching, can only be tried (R5, TRL 4)
check: 12 N (Janssen) and 45 N (hydrostatic upper bound) against a 50 N comfortable crank force; jamming not analysed

claim: The track end stops take the deck running into them at walking-wheel speed (the design basis; a runaway on a slope or in a gale is held by the lock pin and the storm clamps, not by the stops)
law: Kinetic energy at one hand wheel turn a second absorbed over 10 mm of rubber, two stops; two M12 8.8 in shear with a partial factor of 1.5; the track under a stop is held only by pad friction (about 2.4 kN), so it creeps along the wall when struck and its gauge is checked after any impact

claim: No piece carried up the kiln weighs more than 40 kg (R12)
law: Masses from the model solids (S275 7,850 kg/m3); the margin is under 1 %, and mill tolerance on hollow sections, weld metal and paint can add several per cent, so the pieces are weighed before they go up (TRL 4) and D14 (shorter modules) is the real fix

claim: A heel load on a floor panel is carried by the frame and the board
law: Edge angles 98 MPa against 275 MPa; board under a 60 mm heel 0.41 MPa; board strength from the supplier (KND-DEC-001, item 4)
check: Frame within yield; board compressive strength at least 0.6 MPa to confirm when bought

claim: Every part of the detailed model can be made and fitted as drawn (kit 1.9 D3)
law: Solid interference between every pair of parts more than 5 mm3 (cad_check.py); first D3 model: cleat bolts through the chord, chain drive through the fork carrier, pillow blocks under the end bearer, gate leaf on the post bolt heads
check: Fixed by KND-DEC-001 D13; cad/fidelity.json reports no interference in either option; a zero-interference model is not a fit-up (weld distortion, clearances and tolerances) and is confirmed by a trial assembly (TRL 4)

claim: The deck stays put on its track in a pre-monsoon storm when it is not being worked
law: Drag 0.5 rho Cf A v^2 on 6.1 m2 (Cf 2.0) at a 28 m/s storm gust (5.8 kN; 28 m/s is 100 km/h, the lower end of the 'over 100 km/h at times' of Banglapedia, so a design gust is a decision for the partner and a local code); before D12 the lock pin alone held to 10 m/s; with D12 there are four chains, two of which resist each direction; the check counts the chains alone (the pads slide at 4.8 kN, so clamps and pads are not relied on)
check: Chain tension 5.3 kN at 28 m/s against 19.6 kN working load limit; the chains alone reach it at a 54 m/s gust; the anchors are the unknown (S21)

claim: The tie-down anchors hold in the ground beside the kiln
law: Each anchor resists 5.3 kN at 28 m/s (about 10 kN at 38 m/s) against a 19.6 kN chain working load limit (8 mm grade 80, EN 818-2); screw anchor pull-out depends on the yard soil and the sideways pull on the derailment guards and wall tops is to confirm
check: Anchor pull-out to assess at the partner kiln (survey)

claim: Two people can carry every piece up the kiln within the team-handling guide
law: ISO 11228-1 reference mass 25 kg; HSE L23: a two-person team handles about two-thirds of the sum of their capabilities (33.3 kg); the 3 m track modules (33.4 kg) are also just over it, and a carry up a ramp in heat lowers the limit further; fix proposed to Amish (KND-DEC-001 D14: five truss modules a side and 2.4 m track modules, all pieces 33 kg or less)

claim: The storm wind does not lift the parked deck off its track (gust of 28 m/s)
law: Dynamic pressure 0.5 rho v^2 x plan area 7.7 m2 x a lift coefficient of 1.0 (an upper bound, assumed; no source found) against the deck weight (the clamps and chains add to it); added after the independent review of 2026-10-29

claim: The 10 mm carrying rope carries the full bucket with a factor of 5
law: Span 6,400 mm between lugs, trolley 1,800 mm from the outer lug; rope tension = P a b / (L sag) + w L^2 / 8 sag with a 150 mm sag; 32 kg x 1.25; minimum breaking load about 56 kN (catalogue)

claim: The guyed mast does not buckle
law: Euler buckling of SHS 100 x 100 x 5, 2.4 m, K = 2 (conservative); the limit shown is the buckling load divided by 3

claim: A 7.5 m/s wind does not swing the hanging bucket off the feed hole
law: Drag on the bucket against its weight; offset at a 1 m hang; the bucket is positioned over a hole only when it holds fuel
check: 13 mm with a full bucket (26 kg); the empty 8 kg bucket swings 41 mm, over the 25 mm, so it is raised before the wind can move it (the independent review found 60 to 95 mm for a nearly empty bucket with pendulum overshoot); to try at TRL 4

claim: One fireman feeds 18 holes in a 17.5 min round from the wall top
law: Trolley out 3 m at 0.5 m/s, lower, tip and raise 30 s, back 6 s, refill share 10 s; the round allows 58 s a hole
check: 52 s a hole against 58 s allowed, a 12 % margin on assumed task times with no rest allowance in 45 C heat; a time-and-motion trial would settle it

claim: The skids and guys can be moved 1 m along the kiln for each row of holes
law: Sliding a 120 kg skid at friction 0.4 takes about 470 N (two people); every move needs three guy anchors per mast reset and retensioned
check: Within known science; the reset of six anchors every row is the option's main practical risk (KND-OPT-001)
